newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila property firms lead gainers by late trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila property firms lead gainers by late trade.

text.p: Two Philippine low-cost housing developers led a group of rising secondliners in late trade as investors positioned themselves ahead of release of first quarter GNP data later this week, brokers said.
"It seems that there's positioning for a favourable GNP figure," one trader from a local brokerage house said.
She said retail and some foreign institutional investors were slowly nibbling at active secondliners, such as C&P Homes Inc and Filinvest Land Inc, after speculating on thirdliners late last week.
C&P Homes gained 50 centavos or 5.43 percent to 9.70 pesos. Filinvest also went up 50 centavos or 9.25 percent to 5.90 pesos.
A Reuters poll showed that analysts expect GNP to ease slightly to 6.34 percent in the first quarter of the year against last year's 6.6 percent.
The projected rate is still above 6.0 percent threshold level which many analysts pegged as an acceptable level for the country to reach its full-year target of 7.0 to 8.0 percent.
